newsitem.title: USA: U.S. economy growing quite strongly - Fed's Meyer.
newsitem.headline: U.S. economy growing quite strongly - Fed's Meyer.

text.p: The U.S. economy is growing strongly at a rate well above its long-term trend, Federal Reserve Governor Laurence Meyer said Thursday.
"The economy is growing quite strongly," he told the central bank's Consumer Advisory Council.

Growth in the first quarter looks to have been close to a four percent annualized pace, he said. That is nearly twice the economy's generally perceived trend growth rate of 2 to 2-1/2 percent, he added.

"The economy is growing at a healthy rate, but at a rate above its sustainable rate. We're very close to capacity, at or maybe slightly beyond," Meyer said, noting that the unemployment rate is at about a seven-year low.
Wages have begun to rise, but inflation to date remains "remarkably well-behaved," he said.
"When the economy grows above trend, utilization rates increase," Meyer said. "At some point you increase excess demand ... and that's what you have to worry about."
Meyer warned of the risk of pushing the unemployment rate down too far below a threshold that would stir inflation.
"We want maximum sustainable levels of employment," Meyer said.
"There is a threshold out there for the unemployment rate. If you go beyond that you get higher and higher inflation ... We're not prepared to tolerate that," he said.
